"""Synthetic upstream app.py for tests/test_route_drift.py.

This file is parsed with ast only. It is never imported or executed, which is
why it carries a .txt suffix. Each route element is labelled with the
requirement 2 form it exercises and the guard verdict the tests expect.
"""

from starlette.applications import Starlette
from starlette.routing import Route

_DOCS = {
    "/skill.md": "synthetic skill text",
    "/interop.md": "synthetic interop text",
}


def _get_write(path, endpoint):
    route = Route(path, endpoint)
    route.methods = {"GET"}
    return route


app = Starlette(
    routes=[
        # (d) literal tuple comprehension: covered static documents.
        *[Route(path, llms_txt) for path in ("/", "/llms.txt")],
        # (e) _DOCS comprehension: /skill.md covered, /interop.md uncovered.
        *[Route(path, doc_md) for path in _DOCS],
        # (a) covered static document.
        Route("/healthz", healthz),
        # (a) uncovered static document.
        Route("/stats", stats),
        Route("/rooms", rooms),
        Route("/r/{room}", room_read),
        # (b) merged with the GET entry above.
        Route("/r/{room}", room_post, methods=["POST"]),
        # (a) uncovered parameterised read.
        Route("/r/{room}/export", room_export),
        # (b) POST that the guard does not call a write.
        Route("/r/{room}/archive", room_archive, methods=["POST"]),
        # (c) GET-shaped write that the guard covers.
        _get_write("/r/{room}/say/{nick}/{text:path}", room_say),
        # (c) GET-shaped write that the guard does not call a write.
        _get_write("/r/{room}/poke/{nick}", room_poke),
    ],
)
